text:
The Kebarrow Compact endured twenty years of internal fragmentation and external predation, its authority eroded by a succession of short-lived rulers and repeated betrayals. The period began with a marriage in year 2 that bound the Compact to the Griwick Compact, but this alliance offered no protection against the Griwick Compact’s own raids. The Compact’s standing fell from its initial position to "very low" by year 15, when Meigate rose against it, a rebellion triggered by the outlawing of Witrou Breim. The seat passed through five holders, three of whom were killed, reflecting a cycle of violence that defined the era.

Reweld Wul took the seat in year 8 after Searn Sisrill was killed by Math Ham. Reweld Wul’s rule ended in year 14 when Witrou Breim, who had returned from exile in year 8, had him murdered. Witrou Breim took the seat by election but lost it in year 15 when Pouldrir Ho challenged him openly and won. Witrou Breim was cast out and later declared an outlaw for conspiracy. Pouldrir Ho ruled until year 20, when Turaer Danpa, who had returned from exile in year 17, had him murdered. Turaer Danpa’s act was a purge within the Compact, as were the murders of Searn Sisrill and Reweld Wul.

Sou Dra took the seat by election in year 20 after Pouldrir Ho’s death. Sou Dra’s rule was tested in year 21 when Thra Bround challenged him openly and lost; Thra Bround was killed by Sou Dra. Throughout the period, the Compact sent eight raids, three of which carried off plunder, while suffering six raids from the Griwick Compact and the Wurn League. The Compact’s internal cohesion failed as four people were courted away from its rulers, and two were cast out for conspiracy or defeat. The period ended in year 21 with Sou Dra still holding the seat, but the Compact’s authority had been significantly diminished by the loss of Meigate and the frequent turnover of its leadership.

The Vea Lode Covenant began in year 29 when Vea Lode broke from the Griwick Compact, with Mothgall Vafarn taking the seat. The new power faced immediate hardship, as famine struck Vea Lode in year 30, leaving grain short and killing 11 people. This disaster initiated a prolonged decline, with the famine continuing for three more years. In year 31, 13 died and 32 abandoned the place. In year 32, 9 died and 22 left. In year 33, 7 died and 30 abandoned the place. The internal stability of the Covenant also fractured during this time. In year 33, Sou Dra had Mothgall Vafarn murdered at Vea Lode. Sou Dra then took the seat by election.

The Covenant shifted from internal survival to external aggression. In year 34, it raided Griwick, carrying off 36 grain and killing 20. In year 35, it raided Laehiford, carrying off 44 grain and killing 28. These raids were followed by another internal purge. In year 36, Bu Rumpirn had Sou Dra murdered at Vea Lode. Bu Rumpirn took the seat by election. He held the position until his death in year 39 at the age of 60.

The period ended with the dissolution of the power. In year 39, the Vea Lode Covenant came to an end. Its single place fell to no one. The succession by election had produced three rulers: Mothgall Vafarn, Sou Dra, and Bu Rumpirn. The initial break from the Griwick Compact did not secure the Covenant’s longevity, as it ended without a successor holding the seat.

The Griwick Compact’s twenty-year span from 4 to 23 was defined by a war with the Wurn League that began in 5 and ended in 18, five years of fighting that consumed the power’s early energy. The conflict started when the Compact declared war for Threi Cut, broke its alliance with the Wurn League, and lost a battle at Threi Cut in 5 with 45 dead. It reversed this defeat by winning three successive battles against the Wurn League at Threi Cut in 6 and 7, and at Laehiford in 8, taking Threi Cut and Laehiford from the League. The war ended in 18 with both sides exhausted. During this period, the Compact sent six raids, all carrying off plunder, and suffered ten raids, six of which were beaten off.

Internal stability fractured under the rule of Kei Leassel, who took the seat in 9 by setting aside the claim of the named heir Turaer Danpa. Kei Leassel had Math Ham murdered at Hadale in 10. His rule ended when he died in 17. Before his death, the Compact’s standing had fallen very low, prompting Vea Lode to rise against it in 9, and fallen to nothing, prompting Threi Cut to rise against it in 12. Three people were cast out during this period: Pouldrir Ho for attempted murder in 9, Turaer Danpa for the losing claim in 9, and Beirn Naem for the losing claim in 17. One exile, Witrou Breim, returned in 17.

Witrou Breim took the seat in 17 after rejecting the rival claim of Beirn Naem. He held the seat until he was killed by Bu Rumpirn at Griwick in 23. Thold Valmaer took the seat in 23 by the strongest claim. The period ended with Thold Valmaer still holding the seat. Four people held the seat in these twenty years, with an average tenure of 4.7 years. The Griwick Compact finished the period with its standing diminished by internal purges and external uprisings, though it retained its territorial gains from the Wurn League.

The Kebarrow Compact’s nineteen-year tenure from 22 to 40 was defined by a relentless war with the Griwick Compact that ended in its destruction. The period began with Sou Dra holding the seat, a position he maintained through open challenges and internal purges until his own ousting. The Compact’s standing eroded through four lost battles, two places lost, and the scattering of its final followers, leaving it finished and landless by the end of the period.

Sou Dra’s rule was marked by internal instability and external aggression. He survived a conspiracy by Turaer Danpa in 25 and another by Theald Va in 28, executing both men. He ordered the murder of Thold Valmaer at Griwick in 28 and Kondruth Tru at Hadale in 37. His authority ended in 29 when Tor Nathgoull challenged him openly, won, and took the seat, casting Sou Dra out. Tor Nathgoull’s rule was brief; he was challenged and defeated by Throll Kell in 32, who took the seat by coup and cast Tor Nathgoull out. Throll Kell held the seat until 35, when Beas Krouthea challenged him openly, won, and took the seat, casting Throll Kell out. Beas Krouthea ruled until 38, when Kou Peis murdered him at Kebarrow.

The war with the Griwick Compact shaped the Compact’s decline. The Kebarrow Compact declared war on the Griwick Compact in 27 over a long-standing grievance. It fought four battles, all lost: at Vea Lode in 27 with 57 dead, at Vea Lode in 28 with 48 dead, at Kebarrow in 38 with 142 dead, and at Kebarrow in 39 with 118 dead. The Compact sent four raids: one against Griwick in 25 was beaten off, one against Laehiford in 26 carried off plunder, one against Threi Cut in 27 took nothing, and one against Hadale in 35 was beaten off. It suffered one raid on Kebarrow in 26, which carried off plunder. The Compact lost Meigate to the Meigate Covenant in 29 and Kebarrow to the Griwick Compact in 39. Diweith Mound took the seat by election in 38 but was cast out in 39 for an attempted murder. The Kebarrow Compact was finished in 39, its last 9 followers scattering, and peace was made with the Griwick Compact in 40.

The Griwick Compact endured eight years of violent internal turnover and a single, protracted war with the Meigate Covenant. The period began with the murder of Throll Kell by Lorn Waldhith at Griwick in 44, an act that allowed Tum Ga to seize the seat by the strongest claim. Tum Ga’s rule was brief; he was challenged and defeated by Stonand Ker in 45, who took the seat by coup and cast Tum Ga out. The Compact’s stability remained fragile as Lorn Waldhith’s conspiracy against Stonand Ker was uncovered in 45, leading to Lorn’s exile. Stonand Ker’s tenure ended in 47 when Kou Peis murdered him at Hadale. Kou Peis’s own rule was short-lived, ending in 48 when his conspiracy against the new ruler, Thres Thrild, was uncovered and he was executed. Thres Thrild held the seat until 49, when Raes Go challenged and defeated him, taking the seat by coup and casting Thres out. Raes Go’s rule ended in 50 when Paernmel Has openly challenged and defeated him, killing Raes at Griwick and taking the seat. Paernmel Has held the seat as the period closed in 51.

The Compact’s external relations were defined by its conflict with the Meigate Covenant. In 45, the Compact raided Meigate, killing 29 but taking nothing. In 47, the Meigate Covenant declared war and broke its alliance with the Compact. The Meigate Covenant raided Griwick in 47, carrying off 23 grain and killing 16. The Compact defeated the Meigate Covenant at Threi Cut later that year, with 12 dead. The Compact defeated the Meigate Covenant at Threi Cut again in 48, with 10 dead. The war lasted two years, ending in 49 when both sides made peace, exhausted. The Meigate Covenant raided Laehiford in 49, but the raid was beaten off. In 51, the Meigate Covenant raided Hadale, carrying off 49 grain and killing 14.

Internal cohesion eroded throughout the period. Four people were cast out: Tum Ga and Thres Thrild as the losing side of coups, Lorn Waldhith for conspiracy, and Drouldthas Stour for a losing claim. Three exiles returned to service: Raes Go in 45, Heillvar Maer in 46, and Tor Nathgoull in 49. The Compact suffered four killings from within its own people: Throll Kell, Stonand Ker, Kou Peis, and Raes Go. The Compact ordered one killing against a person of another power: Diweith Mound at Meigate in 46. Six people held the seat in eight years, with an average tenure of 1.1 years. The seat passed five times. The Compact fought two battles, both won. One war was begun.

The Griwick Compact’s twenty-year span from 24 to 43 was defined by violent succession, external warfare, and internal decay. The period began with a coup that displaced Thold Valmaer and installed Bu Rumpirn, who was himself overthrown in the same year. This instability preceded a plague at Griwick that killed 184 people and initiated a sickness cycle lasting five years and claiming 640 lives. The Compact engaged in three wars, defeating the Kebarrow Compact and the Wurn League in six battles, yet it lost Vea Lode to a breakaway covenant and saw two of its settlements rise against it as its standing fell to nothing. The era ended with Throll Kell holding the seat after an open challenge, having taken Kebarrow from the destroyed Kebarrow Compact but suffering raids from the Meigate Covenant.

Succession was rapid and bloody. Thold Valmaer held the seat until 24, when Bu Rumpirn challenged and won, taking the seat by coup. Thold Valmaer challenged back in 24, won, and took the seat, casting out Bu Rumpirn. Thold Valmaer ruled until 28, when he was killed by Sou Dra. Nael War took the seat by the strongest claim. Nael War ruled until 34, when he was killed by Stonand Ker. Kondruth Tru took the seat by the strongest claim. Kondruth Tru ruled until 37, when he was killed by Beas Krouthea. Durnrin Drar took the seat by the strongest claim. Durnrin Drar was killed by Stonand Ker in 41. Heth Fal contested the claim of Sor Pean, the named heir, and took the seat by the strongest claim, casting out Sor Pean. Heth Fal was challenged openly by Throll Kell in 42, who won and took the seat, casting out Heth Fal. Throll Kell held the seat at the end of the period.

The Compact fought the Kebarrow Compact and the Wurn League in a series of conflicts. The Kebarrow Compact raided Griwick in 25, which was beaten off. The Griwick Compact raided Kebarrow in 26, carrying off 47 grain and killing 23. The Kebarrow Compact declared war on the Griwick Compact in 27 over a long-standing grievance. The Griwick Compact defeated the Kebarrow Compact at Vea Lode in 27, killing 57. The Griwick Compact defeated the Kebarrow Compact at Vea Lode in 28, killing 48. The two sides made peace in 29. The Griwick Compact declared war on the Wurn League in 33 over a long-standing grievance. The Griwick Compact defeated the Wurn League at Hadale in 33, killing 58. The Griwick Compact defeated the Wurn League at Hadale in 34, killing 87, and took Hadale from the Wurn League. The Wurn League was finished in 34. The Griwick Compact declared war on the Kebarrow Compact in 38. The Griwick Compact defeated the Kebarrow Compact at Kebarrow in 38, killing 142. The Griwick Compact defeated the Kebarrow Compact at Kebarrow in 39, killing 118, and took Kebarrow from the Kebarrow Compact. The Kebarrow Compact was finished in 39.

Internal cohesion eroded as the Compact expanded. Vea Lode broke from the Griwick Compact in 29 to form the Vea Lode Covenant. Threi Cut rose against the Griwick Compact in 30, when its standing had fallen to nothing. Laehiford rose against the Griwick Compact in 37, when its standing had fallen to nothing. The Griwick Compact suffered 14 raids during the period. It sent out three raids, all carrying off plunder. It ordered one killing against a person of another power: Leimmil Theall at Meigate in 42. One of its own people was murdered from within: Leimmil Theall. Four people were cast out. Two exiles returned. One marriage tied the Compact to the Wurn League in 29.

The Wurn League’s twenty-year span from 2 to 21 was defined by a rapid unraveling of its diplomatic position and a decisive military collapse against the Griwick Compact. At the start, the League held Threi Cut and maintained alliances with both the Kebarrow Compact and the Griwick Compact through six marriages. By the end, it had lost both Threi Cut and Laehiford to the Griwick Compact, fought five battles against them with only one victory, and seen its internal stability shattered by the exile of Reweld Wul and the usurpation of Math Ham. The period closed with Trem Lolkoll holding the seat, but the League’s territorial integrity and external alliances had been severely diminished.

The League began by securing Threi Cut in 2 and binding itself to its neighbors through marriage. Witrou Breim married Beirn Naem in 3, linking the League to the Griwick Compact, while Teapeall Heampim married Thra Bround in 3, linking it to the Kebarrow Compact. Math Ham married Bu Rumpirn and Trem Lolkoll married Turaer Danpa in 4, further tying the League to the Griwick Compact. These bonds did not prevent conflict. In 4, the Kebarrow Compact raided Laehiford, taking 29 grain. In 5, the Wurn League raided Kebarrow but took nothing, prompting a retaliatory raid by the Kebarrow Compact on Threi Cut. That same year, the Griwick Compact declared war on the League for Threi Cut and broke its alliance. The League defeated the Griwick Compact at Threi Cut in 5, killing 45, but the war continued.

The conflict escalated against the League. In 6, the Griwick Compact defeated the League at Threi Cut, killing 35. In 7, the Griwick Compact defeated the League at Threi Cut again, killing 29, and took Threi Cut from the League. The League also lost Laehiford to the Griwick Compact in 8 after a defeat there that killed 107. The Griwick Compact raided Hadale in 8, taking 48 grain. The League’s internal cohesion failed simultaneously. Reweld Wul was cast out in 7 for an attempted murder. Math Ham took the seat in 7 by setting aside the claim of Witrou Breim, who was also cast out. Math Ham was killed in 10 by Kei Leassel. The war ended in 10 after five years. Trem Lolkoll took the seat in 10 by right of birth. The League sent seven raids between 5 and 17; four were beaten off, two took nothing, and one carried off plunder. It suffered five raids, two of which carried off plunder. A famine at Threi Cut in 6 killed 13. The period ended with Trem Lolkoll still holding the seat.

The Meigate Covenant’s twenty-three years from 29 to 51 were defined by a cycle of expansion, internal fracture, and war with the Griwick Compact. The period began with the secession of Meigate from the Kebarrow Compact, establishing Raes Go as the first ruler. The Covenant initially sought stability through marriage alliances, binding itself to the Vea Lode Covenant in 30 and the Griwick Compact in 35. However, these diplomatic ties could not prevent a long-standing grievance from erupting into open war in 47. The conflict drained the Covenant’s resources, leading to military defeats and the loss of its occupied territories, ending with the power exhausted but still holding the seat under Drarka Draernthun.

Raes Go held the seat from 29 until 44, a tenure marked by the return of exiles and a failed challenge. Heillvar Maer returned in 33, followed by Drarka Draernthun and Tor Nathgoull in 35, and Leimmil Theall in 35. The Covenant’s early raids on Griwick in 31 and Laehiford in 33 were beaten off. A famine at Meigate in 38 killed 61 people and left grain short by 7. In 40, a raid on Kebarrow was also beaten off. In 43, Heillvar Maer challenged Raes Go openly for the seat; Raes Go kept the seat and Heillvar was cast out. Raes Go’s rule ended in 44 when Diweith Mound challenged him openly, won, and took the seat, resulting in Raes Go’s exile.

Diweith Mound ruled from 44 until his death in 46. He occupied Vea Lode in 41, a place no one held. The Griwick Compact raided Vea Lode in 42, carrying off 33 ore and killing 2. The Meigate Covenant raided Hadale in 42, carrying off 27 grain and killing 14, and Threi Cut in 43, carrying off 2 grain and killing 1. In 45, the Griwick Compact raided Meigate, killing 29 but taking nothing. Vea Lode rose against the Covenant in 45 as its standing fell to nothing. Diweith Mound was killed by Stonand Ker at Meigate in 46. Drarka Draernthun contested the claim of the named heir Tor Nathgoull; Drarka took the seat, setting aside Tor’s claim, and Tor was cast out.

Drarka Draernthun held the seat from 46 to 51. In 47, the Covenant declared war on the Griwick Compact and broke its alliance. It raided Griwick, carrying off 23 grain and killing 16. The Griwick Compact defeated the Covenant at Threi Cut in 47, killing 12, and again in 48, killing 10. The two sides made peace in 49 after two years of war. The Covenant raided Laehiford in 49, which was beaten off. In 50, Hehum Skul married Ta Poveil, binding the Covenant to the Griwick Compact. The Covenant raided Hadale in 51, carrying off 49 grain and killing 14. The period ended with Drarka Draernthun still holding the seat.

The Wurn League’s fourteen-year span from 22 to 35 was defined by internal fragmentation and external defeat. At the start, the League was bound to the Kebarrow Compact through marriages in 23, 25, and 28, yet its leadership cycled rapidly. Nine people held the seat, passing eight times, with an average tenure of 1.3 years. The period ended with the League finished, its land lost and its followers scattered, following a war with the Griwick Compact that it lost in two battles.

Trem Lolkoll held the seat at the beginning, but his rule was undermined by conspiracies. Befu Seirn’s plot was uncovered in 22, leading to Seirn’s execution. Nael War’s conspiracy was uncovered in 25, resulting in War’s exile. In 26, Gatros Hearn challenged Trem Lolkoll openly, won, and took the seat. Sothkel Sald then challenged Hearn, won, and took the seat by coup, killing Hearn at Hadale. Saern Meastouth challenged Sald, won, and took the seat by coup, killing Sald at Hadale. Meastouth’s rule was short; his attempt on Thold Valmaer failed in 27, and he was cast out. Teapeall Heampim took the seat by right of birth and died in 28. Paernrom Sir contested the claim of the named heir Bu Rumpirn, won by primogeniture, and took the seat, casting out Rumpirn.

The League’s military and diplomatic position deteriorated. It suffered one raid on Hadale in 24 by the Griwick Compact, which carried off 34 grain. Its own raids on Vea Lode in 29, Laehiford in 29, and Threi Cut in 31 were all beaten off. In 30, Stonand Ker had Paernrom Sir murdered at Hadale. Heillvar Maer took the seat by right of birth. In 31, Teillmol Lund’s conspiracy was uncovered, and he was executed. Heillvar Maer’s attempt on Nael War failed in 32, and he was cast out. Drarka Draernthun took the seat by right of birth.

In 33, the Griwick Compact declared war on the Wurn League over a long-standing grievance and broke its alliance with the League. Stonand Ker challenged Drarka Draernthun, won, and took the seat by coup, casting out Draernthun. Thosruld Lul’s conspiracy was uncovered, and he was executed. The Griwick Compact defeated the Wurn League at Hadale in 33, with 58 dead. In 34, Leimmil Theall’s attempt on Stonand Ker failed, and he was cast out. Stonand Ker had Nael War murdered at Griwick. Theall’s conspiracy was uncovered, and he was declared outlaw. The Griwick Compact defeated the Wurn League at Hadale in 34, with 87 dead, and took Hadale from the League. The Wurn League was finished, its last 25 followers scattering. Peace was made between the Griwick Compact and the Wurn League in 35.

Drarka Draernthun took the seat of the Meigate Covenant in 46 after winning an election that set aside the claim of the named heir Tor Nathgoull. The previous ruler, Diweith Mound, had been killed by Stonand Ker at Meigate earlier that year. Tor Nathgoull was cast out as the losing claimant. Drarka held the seat for the remainder of the period, which ended in 51 with him still in power. The seat passed from Diweith to Drarka once inside these years.

The Meigate Covenant declared war on the Griwick Compact in 47 over a long-standing grievance, breaking its alliance and trade with them. The Covenant fought two battles against the Griwick Compact at Threi Cut, losing both: in 47 with 12 dead and in 48 with 10 dead. The war lasted two years, ending in peace in 49 when both sides were exhausted. During the period, the Meigate Covenant sent three raids: one against Griwick in 47 carrying off 23 grain and killing 16; one against Laehiford in 49 that was beaten off; and one against Hadale in 51 carrying off 49 grain and killing 14. No people were courted away from Drarka’s ruler, though he had won Kaes Rou away from the previous ruler in 46. Five exiles returned to take service with the Meigate Covenant between 47 and 50. Hunger at Vea Lode lasted three years, killing two people in total. One marriage tied the Meigate Covenant to the Griwick Compact in 50.

In year 50, Paernmel Has challenged Raes Go openly for the seat of the Griwick Compact and won, taking the position from Raes Go. Later that same year, Paernmel killed Raes Go at Griwick. Tor Nathgoull was raised to steward of the Griwick Compact in year 50.

In year 51, Visal Veill married Treild Haen at Hadale. Paernmel’s child, Gim Raeldrol, was born at Kebarrow in year 51. Voudreirn Wer, Trurkeand Busi, and Ta Poveil each won Bakrei Dea away from the ruler of the Griwick Compact in year 51. The Griwick Compact spent 205 silver buying goodwill for the fifth time in year 51 and was not believed. In year 51, the Meigate Covenant raided Hadale, carrying off 49 grain and killing 14.

The war began in 27 when the Kebarrow Compact declared it on the Griwick Compact over a long-standing grievance. The Griwick Compact defeated the Kebarrow Compact at Vea Lode in the same year, with 57 dead. The Griwick Compact defeated the Kebarrow Compact at Vea Lode again in 28, with 48 dead.

In 28, Sou Dra had Thold Valmaer murdered at Griwick. The Kebarrow Compact and the Griwick Compact made peace in 29 after two years, both sides exhausted.

The Griwick Compact declared war on the Wurn League in year 5 for Threi Cut. The Wurn League defeated the Griwick Compact at Threi Cut in year 5, with 45 dead. The Griwick Compact defeated the Wurn League at Threi Cut in year 6, with 35 dead. The Griwick Compact defeated the Wurn League at Threi Cut in year 7, with 29 dead. The Griwick Compact took Threi Cut from the Wurn League in year 7.

The Griwick Compact defeated the Wurn League at Laehiford in year 8, with 107 dead. The Griwick Compact took Laehiford from the Wurn League in year 8. The Griwick Compact defeated the Wurn League at Hadale in year 9, with 101 dead. The Griwick Compact and the Wurn League made peace in year 10 after 5 years, both sides exhausted.
